items.title: Finite-type Kac–Moody roots descend to simple roots
items.statement: For a finite-type GCM A, every root of g(A) is Weyl-conjugate to a simple root, and there are finitely many roots. Every root space has dimension one, and g(A) is finite-dimensional.
items.strategy: Work componentwise with the positive definite symmetrization B=DA proved by the local trichotomy, using (alpha_i,alpha_j)=d_i a_ij. For a positive root beta=sum m_i alpha_i, positivity of (beta,beta)=sum m_i(alpha_i,beta) gives i with (alpha_i,beta)>0. Thus beta(h_i)>0 is an integer. If beta is not simple, its support contains an index different from i: the local root-space result excludes pure multiples k alpha_i with k>1. The reflected root s_i beta=beta-beta(h_i)alpha_i retains a positive coefficient at that different index. The proved one-sign root decomposition and Weyl root invariance therefore make it positive, and its height is smaller. Induction on the positive integer height reaches a simple root. Negative roots follow by sign and the simple reflection of alpha_i to -alpha_i. Weyl form invariance implies every root has squared length in the finite set {2d_i}. To prove finiteness without a compact-orthogonal-group theorem, let v_i be the basis dual to the alpha_i for the positive form. Cauchy–Schwarz follows directly by minimizing (u-t v,u-t v) over real t. Hence each integer root coefficient satisfies |m_i|^2=|(beta,v_i)|^2<=C(v_i,v_i), where C=max_i 2d_i. Only finitely many integer coefficient tuples meet these finitely many fixed bounds. Existence of the dual basis follows by finite Gaussian elimination since positivity makes B invertible. Weyl transport preserves the one-dimensional simple root spaces. Finally the existing triangular weight decomposition is h plus the root spaces, and dim h=n because A is invertible. Thus dim g=n+|Delta| is finite. No classification, root-string completeness, highest-root theorem, recurrence or external Serre existence theorem is assumed.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 4.3.2, printed pp.63–64, complete proof read; local height descent and dual-basis lattice bound replace its compact-group route

items.title: Nonsingular indecomposable Kac–Moody algebras are simple
items.statement: If A is an indecomposable GCM with det A nonzero, then g(A) is nonabelian and has no nonzero proper Lie ideal. In particular every indecomposable finite-type component is simple. A Lie ideal means a linear subspace J with [g,J] contained in J; simple here means nonabelian with no nonzero proper ideal.
items.strategy: By the maximal-ideal quotient construction, every nonzero ideal J of g intersects h nontrivially: its inverse image would otherwise be an ideal disjoint from h larger than the defining maximal one. Let 0!=h in J intersect h. Since A is nonsingular, the n independent simple roots form a basis of h-star (dim h=n), so alpha_i(h)!=0 for some i. Then [h,e_i]=alpha_i(h)e_i puts e_i in J, [e_i,f_i]=h_i puts h_i in J, and [h_i,f_i]=-2f_i puts f_i in J. If a_ij!=0, [h_i,e_j]=a_ij e_j puts e_j in J, hence also h_j and f_j. The graph whose edges are nonzero off-diagonal entries is connected by indecomposability, so a finite path repeats this argument at every index. The h_i span h because A is nonsingular. All defining generators lie in J, so J=g. The simple sl2 triple is nonzero by Cartan injectivity and the root-space construction, showing g is nonabelian. This proves simplicity directly rather than invoking a classification or a radical theorem.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 1.4.8(i), printed pp.19–20, complete simplicity argument read

consumer_statement: For a finite-type Cartan matrix A over C, g(A) is finite-dimensional and is a direct sum of nonabelian simple Lie algebras, one for each indecomposable component (thus semisimple). Its simple-root/coroot pairing is A, with rows indexing coroots. Its Cartan–Serre presentation identifies it, generator for generator, with the finite-type Serre-presentation model used by DG-31; this proves existence locally and does not assume the future classification theorem.
consumer_strategy: The local finite-type trichotomy gives symmetrizability, a positive definite symmetrization and rank A=n, hence h=span(h_i). The root-descent lemma proves finite dimension. For each indecomposable component the simplicity lemma proves the associated algebra is nonabelian simple. For different components the Cartan relations and zero-entry Serre relations give zero brackets for every pair of generators (e_i,e_j), (f_i,f_j), (e_i,f_j) and (h_i,h_j), as well as the mixed Cartan-root brackets. Jacobi then makes the generated component subalgebras commute. The local symmetrizable Serre theorem identifies g(A) with the universal algebra of these relations. Mapping each generator into its component gives a homomorphism to the direct sum of the component presentations, and inclusions of the component generators give the reverse homomorphism. Their composites fix all generators, hence are identities. This proves the direct-sum assertion, not merely a quotient of a direct sum. The existing root decomposition, one-sign property and root descent identify the simple roots and their matrix alpha_j(h_i)=a_ij. For any DG-31 model defined by the same full Cartan–Serre generators and relations, the two presentation maps are likewise inverse on all generators. No external theorem is needed to assert its existence or equality as a presented algebra; the classification of the list of finite Dynkin diagrams remains future DG-31 work and is not a premise of this construction. No new pair and no unproved DG-31 dependency are introduced. The statements of simplicity and semisimplicity are explicit above, so no unprovided radical criterion is used.
